newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran forces hit mock enemy in largest Gulf wargame.
newsitem.headline: Iran forces hit mock enemy in largest Gulf wargame.

text.p: Iranian Revolutionary Guards attacked an imaginary enemy in the Gulf on Thursday with ground, naval and air power in mock battles in the Islamic republic's largest wargames.

State-run Tehran radio said paratroopers, backed by planes and helicopter gunships, landed behind "enemy" lines near the port of Bandar Abbas at the mouth of the Gulf, surrounding the "aggressors" and taking them prisoner.

Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who is also armed forces commander-in-chief, urged the troops to take part in the mock battles as if it they were real, "even though...the probability that events such as these wargames would actually occur is very low", the radio said.
He was talking as troops were preparing to land on Iran's Qeshm and Hengam islands to confront an occupying "enemy".
Khamenei on Tuesday urged Iranians to be vigilant but added that no world power would dare attack Iran because, he said, enemies knew Iran's government enjoyed wide popular support.

The remarks were an apparent reference to reports that the United States might strike at the country if a link was established between Tehran and a bombing in June that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia. Iran denies involvement.

A U.S. Navy official in the Gulf earlier on Thurday said the navy was watching the exercises closely, dismissing a Tehran report that U.S. warships had left regions near Iranian waters since the start of the wargames.
"We have changed nothing," the U.S. Navy official said. "As at any time during an exercise we are watching it very closely and we can do that in a variety of means, not just ships.
"The Fifth Fleet has not changed its operations as a result of the exercise. As of this morning there are still 20 ships assigned to the Fifth Fleet," he told Reuters.
The U.S. navy keeps a force of about 20 warships in the Gulf to enforce sanctions on Iraq and protect Gulf Arab oil states.

The amphibious wargames, codenamed "Tariq ol-Qods" (Road to Jerusalem), involve 200,000 members of the guards, set up after Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution, and Basij militia volunteers. Tehran has been training the guards to become a rapid deployment force.
Planned since last year, they are designed to test ability to counter simultaneous threats in Iran's west and south.
They cover 2,000 km (1,200 miles) across four provinces stretching from the mouth of the Gulf to the border with Iraq, Iran's enemy in an eight-year war which ended in 1988.

Tehran radio said people chanting "Death to America" held a rally on Thursday in a desert region in central Iran to mark a failed U.S. military mission in 1980 to free 52 Americans held hostage by Islamic militants at the U.S. embassy in Tehran.
The U.S. operation was aborted after a helicopter collided with a transport aircraft, killing eight U.S. servicemen, during a sandstorm in the desert location.
